newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh ready to repatriate refugees from India.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh ready to repatriate refugees from India.

text.p: Bangladesh said on Monday it was ready with money and logistics to repatriate thousands of refugees from northeast India, where they fled to escape a tribal insurgency in Bangladesh.
"We are ready with money and other support needed to rehabilitate the tribal refugees," said Mohammad Ismail, deputy commissioner of Khagrachhari district in the Chittagong Hill Tracts.
Officials said 6,700 refugees were expected to return to their homes in the Hill Tracts over a week beginning on Friday, in the first phase.

Once they are resettled, tribal leaders now staying in refugee camps in India's Tripura state would visit the Hill Tracts to see if the rehabilitation was satisfactory, and then set a date for the next phase, the officials said.
The mass outflux was triggered by a bloody insurgency by tribal Shanti Bahini guerrillas who demanded autonomy for the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma.
The guerrillas also pressed the government to expel some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the Hill Tracts, which the Shantis consider as a tribal homeland.

More than 8,500 civilians, rebels and security soldiers have been killed in the insurgency since 1973. The fighting also forced some 50,000 tribespeople to flee across the border, according to official figures.

The government has so far refused to pull out the settlers or ease military presence in the region, issues that apparently blocked recent moves for a peace deal between between the government and the rebels.
"Both sides appeared too rigid on the issues," one Hill Tract official said on Monday.
The government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has attached priority to finding a political settlement of the Hill Tracts problems, officials said.
"The ice has started melting," one official said without elaborating.
Ismail said the Tripura government had also taken necessary measures to send home the Bangladeshi refugees. "Good amounts of goodwill exists on both sides," he told Reuters.

The first group of refugees would arrive at Ramgarh, a Hill Tracts border town on March 28, and be received by the government's chief representative, Abul Hasanat Abdullah, a senior leader of the ruling Awami League.
Reception camps have been set up and local officials had funds to pay each refugee family 15,000 taka ($350) in cash.
The refugees will also be given house building materials and food rations for nine months, government officials said.
Around 5,000 refugees were repatriated in February 1994 before the process was stopped abruptly. About 2,000 others have since come back on their own. ,
